steps.decide: What the palette is for: navigation, actions, or both, and what it may not do
How results rank, and why recency and permissions outrank fuzzy score
How focus, the dialog contract and the return path work
How an async search stays honest under fast typing

rules.statement: The palette is an accelerator for people who already know the product; it never becomes the only route to a feature, and every command exists somewhere visible.
Ranking is permission-filtered first, then exact prefix, then fuzzy match, then recency — and the list never shows a command the reader cannot run.
The palette is a modal dialog with its input focused on open, arrows move the active option, Enter runs it, Escape closes and returns focus to whatever had it before.
The query is debounced about 150 ms, each request carries a sequence id, and a slower earlier response never replaces the newer result list.
A destructive command is never the default active option, is labelled with the object it affects, and asks for confirmation rather than running on Enter.
Each row states its scope (where the command applies) and its shortcut, so two commands with the same name are distinguishable before one is run.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: requests carry a sequence id and only the newest may paint; a response for a superseded query is discarded even if it arrives later

sections.intent: Let someone who knows where they are going get there in two keystrokes, without becoming the only door into the product.
useCases: jump to a record by name
nicheDifferences: Palettes are loved by power users and dangerous as the only navigation, because they require knowing the name of the thing
The discipline is permissions-first ranking and never hiding a feature behind a command
